# spyro eval

Evaluate a PHP expression on the remote Laravel server (PHP only).

## Before you run it

PHP only. Boots Laravel (`bootstrap/app.php`) and evaluates one expression; needs `artisan = true`. Use `--json` for machine-readable stdout (progress goes to stderr). On a `sudo = true` profile it runs as `sudo_user`; `--no-escalate` runs as the SSH user. For shell, Python, Node or Docker use `spyro run`. Prefer `eval` over `tinker -e`: no PsySH quoting problems.

Read `spyro profiles` first for hosts and `remote_path`; the `spyro` skill has the safety rules.

## Reference (from `--help`)

### `spyro eval`

```text
Usage: spyro eval [OPTIONS] EXPRESSION

  Evaluate a PHP expression on the remote Laravel server (PHP only).

  For shell commands, Python, Node or Docker use ``spyro run``.

  Boots Laravel via bootstrap/app.php and evaluates the expression directly with php CLI (no PsySH).
  By default, registers PsySH-style short aliases (``DB``, ``Schema``, ``Cache``, model classes,
  etc.) so you can use short class names. Use ``--no-aliases`` to require full namespaces.

  Outputs the result reliably. Avoids the quoting and output-capture issues of `spyro tinker -e`.

  Examples:

    spyro eval 'User::count()' -p staging

    spyro eval 'DB::table("users")->count()' -p staging --json

    spyro eval 'BillExchange::where("enabled", true)->count()' -p staging

Options:
  --json              Output as JSON
  --no-aliases        Skip PsySH-style short aliases (require full namespaces)
  --no-escalate       Don't use sudo
  -p, --profile TEXT  Profile name  [required]
  --help              Show this message and exit.
```
